name: _enter_buffered_busy
reason: BC2.enter (BufC.lean:106) mirrors only the owner check of :298-302 (the blocking and finalizing acquire of :304-325 are out by the single-thread scope); LockDiscipline quantifies over every section m and is closed by rfl, so it restates the definition of BC2.locked/enter/leave and says nothing about whether any C section actually releases the lock on its paths.

name: buffered_clear
reason: no-behaviour applies by the tp_clear policy: two Py_CLEARs plus self->ok = 0, a guard that only matters to code running after tp_clear (the note should mention it; it turns later calls into ValueError instead of a NULL dereference).

name: buffered_traverse
reason: GC traversal (Py_VISIT of the type, raw and dict), no-behaviour by the stated policy.

name: _io__Buffered_simple_flush_impl
reason: BC2.simpleFlush returns None, but the body returns whatever raw.flush() returns (measured on 3.15.2: a raw whose flush returns 42 gives BufferedReader.flush() == 42); and in the crash counterexample it is only the flush inside detach, so any flush that succeeds still refutes BufferedCNoCrash.

name: buffered_closed
reason: bufferedClosed mirrors CHECK_INITIALIZED_INT, GetAttr and IsTrue (Bool-valued), but neither property states its result: both counterexamples still refute with a buffered_closed that calls raw.closed and returns 0 whatever it answers, or that skips CHECK_INITIALIZED_INT.

name: _io__Buffered_detach_impl
reason: BC2.detach follows :622-629 (CHECK_INITIALIZED, _PyFile_Flush through the type's flush, raw = NULL, detached, ok = 0; the re-entrant NULL return is modelled as SystemError); the detachingRaw counterexample turns on exactly its unlocked raw = NULL, and the SIGSEGV reproduces on 3.15.2 and main (caveat: the returned raw object is modelled as None).

name: _buffered_raw_tell
reason: rawTell/checkPos mirror :787-801 (TypeError for str, ValueError from PyNumber_AsOff_t, the invalid-position OSError, abs_pos), but it runs only in __init__, whose error is cleared, in all three counterexamples, so no property constrains its result.

name: _buffered_raw_seek
reason: rawSeek mirrors :811-834 (CallMethodObjArgs NULL check, result checks); RandomFailedSeekTwins only needs the C tell to differ from _pyio's 0, so a raw_seek that changed state before raising, or any C value other than 0, still refutes it.

name: _buffered_init
reason: Folded into BC2.init (size check, allocation bound, cleared raw_tell, abs_pos left at 0), but the three refutations hold for any init that succeeds; nothing states the size <= 0 refusal or the cleared tell failure.

name: _PyIO_trap_eintr
reason: trapEintr tests the class name InterruptedError, but :882-897 test isinstance OSError and errno == EINTR: measured on 3.15.2, a readinto raising InterruptedError('x') propagates (no retry) while PermissionError(errno.EINTR, 'x') is retried, the opposite of the model in both cases; RawReadChecks part 3 inherits this (the harness only raises InterruptedError(EINTR, 'x')).

name: _io__Buffered_read_impl
reason: BC2.read follows :998-1023 (CHECK_INITIALIZED, n < -1, CHECK_CLOSED before the lock, read_all or read_fast then read_generic under the lock); BufferedCNoCrash is refuted on read(1) because nothing re-checks ok after the CHECK_CLOSED callback, reproduced (SIGSEGV) on 3.15.2 and main, duplicate of gh-154997.

name: _io__Buffered_read1_impl
reason: BC2.read1 follows the 3.15.2 body (n < 0 before CHECK_CLOSED, have > 0 fast path, flush, reset, PyBytesWriter_Create, raw read, FinishWithSize(r)); BufferedReaderNoUninit is refuted because :1091 keeps r bytes of a writer the lying raw never filled (caveat: on 3.15.2 that byte happened to read b'\x00'; the reproducer shows the same defect through read() and peek()).

name: _buffered_readinto_generic
reason: BC2.readinto/readintoLoop mirror :1101-1173 closely, but its only entry compares success with toBool: any C readinto that succeeds on the counterexample (returning 0, or the wrong bytes) still refutes BufferedReaderReadintoTwins, so nothing states the count or the bytes it copies.

name: _io__Buffered_readinto_impl
reason: One-line forward to _buffered_readinto_generic(self, buffer, 0); the readinto-twins refutation pins only that the C call succeeds, which a wrong readinto1 flag would also satisfy on that input.

name: _io__Buffered_tell_impl
reason: BC2.tell mirrors :1340-1350 (no lock, raw_tell minus RAW_OFFSET, GH-95782 clamp), but RandomFailedSeekTwins only needs C's tell to differ from _pyio's 0, so any nonzero C tell still refutes it; nothing states the value 2.

name: _io__Buffered_seek_impl
reason: BC2.seek mirrors :1368-1453 (whence check with SEEK_DATA/HOLE, CHECK_CLOSED, check_seekable, the unlocked in-buffer fast path, flush, RAW_OFFSET, raw_seek, reset) with ints only, but the failed-seek refutation is a defect of _pyio and holds for any C seek whose later tell is not 0 (for example one that drops the buffer before the raw seek).

name: _bufferedreader_reset_buf
reason: read_end = -1; it runs only incidentally in __init__ and before fills, and both refutations hold for any reset.

name: _io_BufferedReader___init___impl
reason: BC2.init answers raw.readable() from a Bool flag with no callback, so it cannot express C's `res != Py_True` test (measured: readable() returning 1 is refused by io, accepted by _pyio, a twin difference merged into one flag) or a readable() that raises or re-enters; and every refutation holds for any constructor that succeeds.

name: _bufferedreader_raw_read
reason: BC2.rawRead follows :1628-1669 (NULL view, retry loop, None, PyNumber_AsSsize_t failure, range check, abs_pos); RawReadChecks pins the count range, every int answer exactly and the retry, and the crash counterexample dies at its :1640 call through NULL raw (caveats: the honest-bytes count is not pinned separately, and the retry inherits trapEintr's class test).

name: _bufferedreader_fill_buffer
reason: fillBuffer mirrors :1675-1686, but in both counterexamples it is only the caller of the crashing or succeeding raw read; no property states read_end/raw_pos after a fill or its return value.

name: _bufferedreader_read_fast
reason: readFast mirrors :1786-1794, but it only returns None on an empty buffer in the crash case and is unconstrained in readinto-twins (C success only); no property states its result.

name: _bufferedreader_read_generic
reason: readGeneric mirrors the 3.15.2 body (one unreachable difference: when the fill loop exits with remaining > 0 it returns the written bytes where :1888 returns Finish(writer)), but in both counterexamples it only reaches a fill; nothing states the bytes it returns.

name: _bufferedwriter_reset_buf
reason: write_pos = 0, write_end = -1; run only incidentally (init, empty flush) in the failed-seek case, which holds for any reset.

name: _bufferedwriter_raw_write
reason: BC2.rawWrite follows :1983-2020 (retry loop, None, no PyErr_Occurred check so a failed conversion becomes 'invalid length -1'); RawWriteChecks pins the range and every int answer, including -1 for ints past Py_ssize_t, measured on 3.15.2 (caveats: the honest-count path and the EINTR retry are not stated).

name: _bufferedwriter_flush_unlocked
reason: flushUnlocked mirrors :2028-2076, but the failed-seek counterexample only takes the empty-buffer goto end; no property exercises the rewind, the write loop, the BlockingIOError or the partial-write state.

name: bufferedrwpair_traverse
reason: GC traversal of the type, dict, reader and writer, no-behaviour by the stated policy.

name: bufferedrwpair_clear
reason: tp_clear that only Py_CLEARs reader, writer and dict, no-behaviour by the stated policy.

name: _io_BufferedRandom___init___impl
reason: Seekable, readable and writable are flags answered without a callback, so C's exact `is True` checks (seekable() returning 1 is refused by io, accepted by _pyio, measured) and failing or re-entering inquiries are not expressible; the failed-seek refutation holds for any constructor that succeeds.
